messages.author: 01f32dcbb5507b45
messages.subject: reliability of noe vist for occu
parts:
Hi all,

I am working with a databse of introduction success of turtles in several countries, so I have 0, 1 values. However, it seems clear that several successes are not recorded and I was wondering if I can apply an occupancy model to estimate the true proportion of introduction success events as well as the probability of detecting such events. I have sampling effort as a covariate for detactability and some other covariates for success.

The problem is that I only have one visit, so I do not know how robust the approach of modelling occupancy is with only one visit. Is it possible to compute it at all? Will the results be meaningful?

Any advice will be welcome.

Thanks in advance, best regards

Pablo

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] reliability of noe vist for occu
parts:
hi Pablo,

 

I find that this is an interesting application for occupancy modeling and, btw, it is the „opposite“ of what people have done for estimating the proportion of sites where some species is still extant among a list of sites that were known to be occupied at some earlier time („revisitation studies“, mostly for plants). If you have a list of sites where a species was released over some time period (say, >20 sites) AND replicated surveys, then you can estimate the reintroduction success as the occupancy parameter in the occupancy model. However, without replication, this is not possible.

 

There is an alternative framework for occupancy estimation with single reps and strong covariate information which you may want to look into; see a series of papers by Lele, Moreno, Solymos.

 

Kind regards  ----  Marc

messages.subject: RE: AW: [unmarked] reliability of noe vist for occu
parts:
Thanks for the answer Marc. I have already though on searching for information on repated introductions, but the data on success is relatively scarce, particularly for some countries, so I cannot have several visits. The approach of Lele et al is quite good, but I still have the problem that I should include genera as a random factor. While I can try to fit Mackenzie's model in WinBUGS I am not really aware of how to write the Lele's models in WinBUGS.

Thanks again

Pablo
